title: Simulating the Evolution of Sacrificing for Family
beats: Genes as gamblers: copies can't see each other, so helping relatives is a bet
Names Hamilton's rule, warns its simplicity deceived the presenter, challenges viewer to spot the coming error
Dice game: pay 1, win 7 on a six; enumerate all six outcomes as payout-cost equations
Average the cases, then name it expected value
One blob beats prediction; more blobs make the average converge
Generalize to b*p - c; note it already resembles Hamilton's rule
Reuse blob forest/predator/home world from green-beard video; run baseline
Add alarm-call altruism vs cowardice gene; caveat that behaviour is not one gene
Asks viewer to predict using expected value before running
Altruism wins; explained with b=2, p=1, c=1; 30 runs to try to disprove
Admits asexual case wasn't really a gamble; add sexual haploid reproduction
Best/worst-case reasoning: EV never negative, presenter bets on altruism
Sim shows stalemate; 'you caught me', prediction was wrong, code checked
Viewer gets a minute; reveal r is not p but probability of identity by descent
Frequency framing: added batch must be more orange than current population (50% then 90% examples)
Split p: non-IBD part mirrors population so is neutral; IBD part is r
b*r-c = 0 explains stalemate; drop death to 95% and rule holds
Rough runs can still go extinct; list open questions; tease non-kin cooperation

metrics.misconception: yes: r is the probability another carries the allele (p); presenter planted and committed to it himself
metrics.brute_force: yes 2:10: enumerate all six dice outcomes before averaging
metrics.examples: 4: dice game -> asexual sacrifice -> sexual haploid sacrifice (fails) -> 95% death variant (verifies)
metrics.ending: verified fix, honest list of untested cases, teaser for reciprocal altruism

new_moves.name: planted-error-challenge
new_moves.what: Announce up front that a mistake is coming and dare the viewer to catch it before reveal

new_moves.name: bounded-reasoning
new_moves.what: When a quantity varies, reason from start/best/worst cases instead of solving

new_moves.name: seek-disconfirmation
new_moves.what: Repeat runs explicitly to try to prove yourself wrong

theory: The video teaches by building a plausible-but-wrong model with full viewer buy-in, committing to a prediction, and letting the simulation break it. Because the viewer has used the expected-value tool three times, the failure lands as surprise rather than confusion, and the fix (r vs p, frequency not count) is anchored to a concrete stalemate graph.
velocity: Orchestrator: allow a 'planted-error' playbook where the tutor commits to a naive model, announces a trap, and lets the sim refute it
Scene builder: support multi-run ensemble plots (thin lines + thick average) as the default verification visual
Learner model: before reveal, ask learner to predict and log commitment; score whether they spotted the flaw
Voice: model honest caveats ('I was deceived too') to normalize being wrong
Evals: check that new notation (r) is introduced only after the concept failure motivates it
